scenarios.objective: Create field with GID2400, then nola with UID1200, primary field, supplementary audit, home /home/nola and shell /bin/bash. Create the home from supplied /etc/skel-field, including its .profile and welcome.txt with unchanged text/modes and nola:field ownership. Preserve all existing records, templates and other files. Inspect and verify your complete configuration.

steps: Make and verify the requested changes
scenarios.explanation: The new field group makes GID2400 available. Explicit useradd flags give nola stable UID1200, primary field, extra audit, the requested shell/home and no automatic private group. -m with -k copies the supplied field template; children retain text/modes but receive nola's UID and primary GID. Default-template or metadata-only creation does not satisfy the file checks.
hints: The primary group must exist before useradd. Use the supplied UID/GID rather than automatic allocation.
A correct record created with -M still lacks the required home files. -m creates them; -k chooses the task's template.
Use id nola and ls -ln /home/nola to compare memberships and copied numeric ownership. Existing data must remain unchanged.

accounts_teaching.prerequisite_note: Know how to type one terminal command and read a file path. This introduction explains account flags; no host administrator rights or setup are needed.

concepts.title: Names and stable numbers
concepts.text: An account record gives a name a user number (UID), one primary group number (GID), a home path and a shell. Supplementary groups add memberships. These supplied virtual identities are separate from your own desktop account.

concepts.title: A record and a home are different
concepts.text: useradd -m creates a home and copies a supplied skeleton template; -M creates only the account record. -k selects the template when using -m. This task needs the copied files, not only a line in the account database.

concepts.title: Try safely inside the example
concepts.text: After the example passes, userdel -r iva removes that example account and its owned home. Outside files are unaffected. This ungraded experiment shows what was created; re-running the example's useradd command recreates it. Do not re-run groupadd: that group still exists.

example_commands.explanation: Create sample_field with the supplied group number (GID) 4400. The group must exist before a new user's -g can name it.

Create iva: -N avoids an automatic private group; -u gives UID; -g is the primary group; -G lists extra groups; -d records the home; -s records the shell. -m creates/copies the home; -k selects the supplied template. Each value is explicit here.
Inspect iva's user number and primary/extra group memberships. This reads the virtual records; it does not log in as iva.
List the copied home entries with numeric owner/group IDs. -l requests details; -n keeps IDs numeric. The simulator's listing is deliberately smaller than full Linux ls.
Read the copied virtual welcome text; the original template is unchanged.

accounts_teaching.inputs: Use sample_field GID4400, iva UID3200, primary sample_field and extra sample_audit, /home/iva, /bin/bash and /etc/skel-sample. The default sample users and data must remain. These are example values, not the assignment's values.
accounts_teaching.try_change: Run userdel -r iva after it passes: iva and its copied home disappear, but sample_field and all pre-existing data stay. Re-run only the annotated useradd command to repair.

Preserve audit.txt's different group, all outside ownership, other accounts, text and modes. Inspect and verify the current records and files.

accounts_teaching.prerequisite_note: Complete the onboarding activity or review it first. This activity teaches precise group repair; automatic password or login behavior is not involved.

concepts.title: Replace or append deliberately
concepts.text: usermod -G sets the whole extra-group list. Adding -a, as in usermod -aG sample_audit umi, appends while keeping existing memberships. A primary group is separate: lowercase -g changes it, uppercase -G does not.

concepts.title: Primary-group repair has file effects
concepts.text: For this owned home, changing the primary GID updates home entries that still use the old primary GID. The borrowed file follows that group even though another user owns it. Entries with a different group, and every outside file, must retain their ownership.

concepts.title: Read before changing
concepts.text: id USER reports numeric identities and groups; getent group GROUP reads that local group record's explicit extra members. Neither query changes state. Keep records and numeric file ownership distinct when checking your result.

example_commands.explanation: Read umi's primary and supplementary groups before editing. Primary membership is stored separately from the extra-group list.
Create the required new supplementary group with its explicit GID.
Replace the complete supplementary list: retain sample_audit, add sample_reports and remove sample_legacy. Without -a, omitted extra groups are removed.
Change the primary group. Inside umi's owned home, entries with the old primary GID follow it, even when another UID owns an entry. Other-group and outside entries stay as they were.
Inspect numeric groups on the home files. This is a virtual listing; no recursive chown or real files are involved.
Read the supplementary membership projection. A primary member need not appear in this comma-separated list; id shows the complete memberships.

accounts_teaching.inputs: Repair umi to primary sample_review, extras exactly sample_audit and new sample_reports GID4500. Keep every other record and file. The sample home includes another owner's old-group file and a different-group evidence file.
accounts_teaching.try_change: After it passes, run usermod -G sample_reports umi: this drops sample_audit but keeps the primary group and home effects. Restore just the missing extra group with usermod -aG sample_audit umi.

scenarios.title: Retire an account while preserving the right evidence
scenarios.summary: Remove an owned home and unused group, transfer one report, and retain orphan numeric evidence.
scenarios.objective: Retire reed UID1401: remove the account and /home/reed, then remove retired GID2600. Transfer only /srv/shared/delivery.txt to teal:review. Preserve /srv/shared/evidence.log with its original UID1401/audit ownership, text and mode, even though that user name disappears. Keep every other account, group and file unchanged. Verify records and numeric ownership.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Inspect the first failed account or file check. Compare names and numeric IDs, then repair the current records; preserve unrelated entries and retry.
steps: Make and verify the requested changes
scenarios.explanation: The one requested report is transferred to teal:review. userdel -r removes reed and the owned home, while outside evidence remains with numeric UID1401. groupdel retired can then remove the unused group; it does not rewrite outside files. Doing the handover after account deletion is also valid because the new owner still exists. Account absence is not a promise about passwords, live sessions or authentication.
hints: Deleting the record alone leaves the home. The task asks for both account and owned-home removal.
Only delivery.txt changes ownership; outside evidence must retain numeric UID1401. Do not reassign every file belonging to reed.
The retired group cannot be deleted while reed uses it as primary. Equivalent safe command orders are allowed after that dependency is satisfied.

accounts_teaching.prerequisite_note: Review explicit identities and group membership first. This activity teaches retirement and numeric ownership, not password locking, login denial or terminating a live user session.

concepts.title: Deleting a name is not deleting every owned file
concepts.text: userdel removes the account record; adding -r also removes its owned home in this bounded simulator. Outside files are separate. Numeric UID ownership remains on retained files even after that UID has no account name.

concepts.title: Transfer only the requested report
concepts.text: chown USER:GROUP PATH changes one entry's numeric owner/group while retaining bytes and mode. Keep evidence untouched even when its owner name disappears. groupdel removes the unused group record; it is not a recursive file operation.

concepts.title: Inspect the final database and ownership
concepts.text: Use getent passwd NAME for the local account record and ls -ln DIRECTORY for numeric file evidence. The simulator refuses creating a new account with a UID still present in orphan ownership; this is a disclosed practice boundary, not a Linux prohibition.

example_commands.explanation: Read numeric file ownership before deleting any account. A UID/GID on a file is a number; deleting its name does not automatically erase or reassign that file.
Transfer this one report to the existing successor and group. Both fields are explicit; contents and modes stay unchanged. No -R or blanket ownership change is needed.
Remove wren's record and owned home only. The supplied outside evidence remains with its original numeric owner; the simulator does not model mail or running-process checks.
Remove the now-unused primary group after its user is gone. An existing account still using a primary group would prevent deletion.
Inspect the transferred report and the evidence's retained numeric UID. Without a matching account name, numeric ownership can still remain.
Read the surviving successor's passwd-style record. A query for an absent name returns no record and status2; that is expected absence, not a password/login test.

accounts_teaching.inputs: Retire wren UID3401 and sample_retired GID4600. Remove /home/wren, transfer only delivery.txt to noa:sample_review, and retain evidence.log UID3401/sample_audit with the same text/mode. Every other record and file stays unchanged.
accounts_teaching.try_change: After it passes, run chown umi:sample_audit /srv/shared/delivery.txt. Only the report's ownership becomes wrong; the retired records stay absent. Repair with chown noa:sample_review /srv/shared/delivery.txt.

scenarios.title: Handover a team without losing numeric ownership
scenarios.summary: Combine stable group rename, explicit onboarding, metadata, targeted report transfer and retirement.
scenarios.objective: Rename staging to dispatch while retaining GID2700. Create lumi UID1500 with primary dispatch, supplementary audit, /home/lumi, /bin/bash and the supplied /etc/skel-dispatch home files. Store expiry metadata 2026-11-30. Transfer only route.txt in /srv/shared to lumi:dispatch; remove rowan UID1401 and its home, and delete obsolete temps GID2800. Preserve archive.txt's UID1401/audit ownership, survivors' remaining memberships, every other record and all text/modes. Verify the complete handover; no login or password behavior is required.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Inspect the first failed account or file check. Compare names and numeric IDs, then repair the current records; preserve unrelated entries and retry.
steps: Make and verify the requested changes
scenarios.explanation: Renaming staging retains GID2700, so survivors' numeric memberships and existing team file groups remain attached to the same team. The new lumi record/home uses that team and the supplied template. Only the active report changes UID; historical archive ownership stays numeric UID1401 after rowan is retired. Deleting temps removes that obsolete supplementary membership from surviving users. Expiry is the specified stored UTC day, not a claim about any authentication method. Every part and all preservation requirements must hold together.
hints: Rename the existing team rather than allocating another GID. Inspect getent group staging and numeric file ownership first.
The successor's home must come from the supplied dispatch template. Create the successor before assigning it the active report; either safe retirement order is allowed afterward.

Store the exact expiry metadata with -e, retire only the requested account/home, then remove temps. Preserve the historical orphan UID and all non-temps memberships; no broad ownership rewrite is needed.

accounts_teaching.prerequisite_note: Complete the three preceding account activities or review their introductions. This capstone adds a stable group rename and explicit expiry metadata; all other tools are already practiced.

concepts.title: Rename a team without changing its identity
concepts.text: groupmod -n NEW OLD changes a group's name, not its GID. Existing primary/supplementary memberships and file groups keep the number. Creating a different group is not equivalent to this team handover.

concepts.title: Expiry is a stored date here
concepts.text: usermod -e YYYY-MM-DD stores an account-expiry date; usermod -e '' USER clears it. This simulator grades the exact metadata only. It has no password database secrets, PAM, actual login or session to test, and clearing a date does not enable authentication.

concepts.title: Preserve the unaffected records and evidence
concepts.text: Combine the earlier creation, targeted chown and retirement tools. The obsolete supplementary group can be removed because nobody uses it as primary. Do not delete the renamed team: the successor needs its existing GID. Keep the historical archive's original numeric UID even after its user is removed.

example_commands.explanation: Inspect the current team name and stable GID4700 before the rename. Existing memberships and file ownership refer to this number.
Rename the team while retaining GID4700. This is not deleting/recreating it: all existing numeric membership and ownership references retain that GID.
Create the explicit successor from the supplied sample template. The previous onboarding lesson explains these flags; use the new team name after renaming it.
Record this exact UTC account-expiry date in local metadata. This exercise neither authenticates a login nor models password locking/PAM. An empty quoted date clears this field.
Transfer just the active handover report to the successor; keep the historical archive's numeric owner unchanged.
Remove the retiring account and its owned home after its active report is handed over. Outside historical data remains.
Remove the obsolete extra group. Its supplementary memberships disappear, while survivors' other group numbers stay the same.

Read the simulated shadow-style record: the account-expiry field stores a UTC day number. The ! sentinel is synthetic and contains no password/hash; other aging fields are empty. This query does not authenticate or establish that a login is allowed.

accounts_teaching.inputs: Rename sample_staging to sample_dispatch at GID4700; create sol UID3500 with primary sample_dispatch, extra sample_audit, /home/sol and the supplied dispatch template. Store expiry 2026-04-20, transfer route.txt to sol:sample_dispatch, retire fawn with its home, remove sample_temps, and preserve other data.
accounts_teaching.try_change: After the example passes, run usermod -e '' sol. Only the stored expiry date becomes missing; files, retirement and group identity stay correct. Repair with usermod -e 2026-04-20 sol. Neither change is a login test.
